name: record_layers
title: What wraps your data on the wire
summary: After authentication each YTP/1 frame is sealed, framed for the carrier and sent as WebSocket data on an HTTP/2 stream inside TLS 1.3.
comment: Checked against docs/protocol/YTP_1.md (frame header, post-AUTH record
protection, H2-duplex carrier framing) and src/providers/h2_duplex_carrier.cpp.

nodes.title: Your data
nodes.note: What the application sent: bytes of a stream, or one whole packet for UDP and TUN.

nodes.title: YTP/1 frame
nodes.note: A 12-byte header names the record type, the stream and the payload length. Frames are what both ends of a session exchange.

nodes.title: Sealed record
nodes.note: The frame is encrypted and authenticated with a key used for this record only, named by its direction, epoch and sequence.

nodes.title: Carrier envelope
nodes.note: Keeps each sealed record whole across partial reads and however WebSocket splits or joins messages.

nodes.title: WebSocket
nodes.note: The carrier speaks ordinary WebSocket, with client frames masked as a browser masks them.

nodes.title: HTTP/2
nodes.note: One RFC 8441 CONNECT stream on a connection that has already loaded the cover site like a browser.

nodes.title: TLS 1.3
nodes.note: The outer encryption, opened with the ClientHello of the pinned Chrome release. An observer sees this layer and its sizes and timing.

nodes.title: TCP
nodes.note: One connection to the server's address, which anyone on the path can see.
